newsitem.title: USA: Freeze damages unknown amount of Oklahoma wheat.
newsitem.headline: Freeze damages unknown amount of Oklahoma wheat.

text.p: A freeze damaged Oklahoma's wheat crop late in the week ended Sunday, but an accurate damage assessment will not be ready until next week, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday.

"Weekend temperatures plunged below freezing for more than 12 hours across much of Oklahoma, causing an undetermined amount of freeze damage to wheat and other small grain crops," the service said in its weekly crop report.
Early planted wheat that was in the latter stage of jointing is highly susceptible to freeze damage if temperatures are 28 degrees or lower for two to four hours.

Wheat condition was rated five percent excellent, 61 good, 25 fair and nine poor, but that did not include the unknown amount of damage. The rating compared to last week's rating of 13 percent excellent, 69 good, 16 fair and two percent poor.
Livestock condition was rated two percent excellent, 76 good, 19 fair and three percent poor. Pasture and range condition was rated four percent excellent, 63 good, 29 fair and four percent poor.
Topsoil moisture was rated 26 percent surplus and 74 percent adequate.
